revised_hierarchy.tier_1_primary: 55-species broad test of a universal migration-to-phenology speed optimum
revised_hierarchy.tier_2_mechanistic: direct phase-control reconstructions in mule deer, barnacle goose and Eurasian wigeon

primary_claim: The registered 55-species macroecological analysis does not support one universal animal-to-environment migration speed optimum.
mechanistic_role: Direct controller systems explain why a universal speed rule fails by showing phase transformation through different actuator architectures and interval scales.
prohibited_interpretations: do not count the three direct taxa as three independent estimates of one universal lambda
do not replace the rejected universal speed rule with a universal raw lambda
do not promote interval-standardized k_eq to a universal biological constant
do not let the Aikens outcome determine whether the 55-species primary result is retained
relationship_to_interval_standardization: compatible_with payoff_b_phase_retention_interval_standardization_v1; raw lambda remains system-specific and secondary standardized coordinates remain descriptive
